9.0.0.en: 1 He cried also in mine ears with a loud voice, saying, "Cause them that have charge over the city to draw near, even every man with his destroying weapon in his hand." 2 And, behold, six men came from the way of the higher gate, which lieth toward the north, and every man a slaughter weapon in his hand; and one man among them was clothed with linen, with a writer's inkhorn by his side: and they went in, and stood beside the brasen altar.

9.1.0.en: These men came "from the way of the higher gate, which lieth toward the north, and every man a slaughter weapon in his hand" [2]. Perhaps their coming from the north is a reference to the Chaldean attack from the direction of Babylon. Or perhaps it is because the seat of the image of jealousy was at the entrance of the inner court that faces north (Ezek 8:3), as though divine chastisement goes forth from the very place where evil is found. As for their being six, perhaps it is because the gates of Jerusalem at that time were six, as though the attack would come from every gate and there would be no way of escape, just as the commanders of the Chaldean army were also six (Jer 39:3). In any case, the number 6 often points to deficiency, which is why the number of the name of the beast is 666, that is, the confirmation of its deficiency three times over. These men, then, only give to the wicked the wages of their evil, which is its natural fruit.

9.2.0.en: 3 And the glory of the God of Israel was gone up from the cherub, whereupon he was, to the threshold of the house. And he called to the man clothed with linen, which had the writer's inkhorn by his side. Among these chastisers there is one who wears priestly garments: "a man clothed with linen, with a writer's inkhorn by his side" [2].

9.2.1.en: In ancient times few knew how to write, so the scribe usually accompanied the important persons who carried out a particular mission, as their secretary. The inkhorn was an animal's horn filled with ink made from the soot of lamps (lampblack) mixed with gum and water, and the scribe wore the inkhorn with its ink at his side. The pen used was of wood or bone. The scribe was always ready to write. He without doubt represents the Lord Christ, who came for our salvation, who poured out blood and water from His pierced side in order to record our names in the Book of Life.

9.2.2.en: When Ezekiel became "a sign to the house of Israel," their iniquities brought paralysis upon him, so that he lay on his side without movement. But the Lord Christ, when He bowed His head to bear our iniquities and to condemn them in His body, it was not possible for death to hold Him nor for sin to cling to Him, and He poured out for us from His side the sacrament of life and eternal salvation! His side was opened so that we may enter into the bowels of His infinite love, and He lifts us up to the bosom of His Father, reconciling us to Him by His precious blood. As the Apostle says: "Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus, by a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh; and having an high priest over the house of God; let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water" (Heb 10:19-22).

9.2.3.en: The six men entered and "stood beside the brasen altar" [2], which is a type of the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ that bears the sacrifice, and in its light the unrepentant are judged. Through the sacrifice the repentant enjoy infinite mercies, and the wicked fall under eternal judgment.

9.2.4.en: "And the glory of the God of Israel was gone up from the cherub, whereupon he was, to the threshold of the house" [3]. The throne of grace has been turned into a throne of judgment; divine grace has been trampled upon and the holiness of God has been offended.

9.3.0.en: "4 And the LORD said unto him, Go through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem, and set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations that be done in the midst thereof" [4].

9.3.1.en: The word "mark" here is Taw, that is, a seal connected with the name of God. For the Lord Christ, when He offered His blood as an atonement for our sins, brought us into the possession of God, so that we carry His name on our foreheads as the sacrament of our sanctification, just as the high priest of old placed a golden plate on his forehead on which was written: "Holiness to the LORD," without which he could not enjoy the divine holy things (Ex 28:36-38). By this we enter into the Father's bosom and are kept safe from destruction. This is the work of the Holy Spirit, with whom we are sealed in the sacrament of the Holy Myron, so that all our members become the possession of the Lord and our souls are kept under His divine protection.

9.3.2.en: The word "mark," or Taw, has drawn the attention of many because it bears the Greek letter Taw, which has the form of the cross. Origen, therefore, speaks of this chapter, saying that the mark is the sign of the cross. Tertullian speaks of it as the sign of the sufferings of the Lord Christ, as a sacrament of salvation from destruction, as he said: [The Greek letter Tau, or our (Latin) letter T, is the very form of the cross, which He foretold would be the sign on the foreheads of the true and Catholic Jerusalem.] This is the sign that keeps the believer, and as St. John Chrysostom says: [You are one of the faithful; make the sign of the cross. Say: This is my only weapon, this is my medicine, I know nothing else.] He also says: [Let the cross be hung above our beds instead of the sword, and let us engrave it on our doors instead of the bolt. And let it be around our houses in the place of a wall.]

9.3.3.en: St. Jerome says: ["Ezekiel says: Set a mark Thaw upon the foreheads of them that sigh, and slay none of those who have the mark; no one who has the sign of the cross on his forehead can be struck by Satan, for he cannot wipe it out; only sin alone can do so.]

9.4.0.en: He says of them: "the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations that be done in the midst thereof" [4]. He did not say that they had not fallen into error, but He affirms their hatred of it and their continual sighing over the abominations. St. Augustine sees that they are a living image of the strugglers who live in the midst of abominations and are exposed to them, yet seek deliverance from them with unceasing sighs. [They sigh and groan; therefore their foreheads were sealed, sealed on the forehead of their inner man, not the outer, for there is a forehead of the conscience as there is of the face... These were marked so that they might not perish, for although they are unable to correct the sins that are committed in their midst, they grieve. This grief itself sets them apart (from the wicked) in the eyes of God, even if in the eyes of men they are mingled with the others. They bear the mark in a hidden way and not openly.]

9.4.1.en: In any case, the book of Ezekiel, which in most of its first chapters focuses on chastisement and punishment, often speaks of the remnant kept for God. It is the story of every generation and a subject of God's care. God did not forget Lot and his family when the sin of Sodom and Gomorrah became exceedingly great and He rained brimstone and fire upon them from heaven (Gen 19), nor did He forget Noah and his family when He drowned the earth with the flood (Gen 6-7), and when Jerusalem, the city of the great King, rejected Him, He found His rest in Bethany during the period of the Passion Week...

9.5.0.en: 5 And to the others he said in mine hearing, Go ye after him through the city, and smite: let not your eye spare, neither have ye pity: 6 Slay utterly old and young, both maids, and little children, and women: but come not near any man upon whom is the mark; and begin at my sanctuary. Then they began at the ancient men which were before the house. 7 And he said unto them, Defile the house, and fill the courts with the slain: go ye forth. And they went forth, and slew in the city. 8 And it came to pass, while they were slaying them, and I was left, that I fell upon my face, and cried, and said, Ah Lord GOD! wilt thou destroy all the residue of Israel in thy pouring out of thy fury upon Jerusalem? 9 Then said he unto me, The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is exceeding great, and the land is full of blood, and the city full of perverseness: for they say, The LORD hath forsaken the earth, and the LORD seeth not. 10 And as for me also, mine eye shall not spare, neither will I have pity, but I will recompense their way upon their head.

9.6.0.en: He says: "Begin at my sanctuary. Then they began at the ancient men which were before the house. And he said unto them, Defile the house, and fill the courts with the slain: go ye forth. And they went forth, and slew in the city" [6-7].

9.6.1.en: The divine command for chastisement was given, to begin with the elders who served in the house of the Lord, and as Origen says: [Judgment begins at the house of God.] And when the Lord called the owners of the talents to account, He began first with the one who had ten talents and ended with the one who had one talent. So God is concerned for the sanctification of those who work in His vineyard, so that they may be a living example to His people; if these behave wrongly, they fall under chastisement before others. Indeed, how greatly the Church needs to care for the sanctification of her priests and of all who work in the house of the Lord before the people, lest they fall into Pharisaism or legalism. They defiled the divine house with idol worship, and here the Lord leaves it defiled with the corpses of the slain within it, those who rebelled against Him.

9.7.s.en: 6. The appearance of the Lord girded:

9.7.0.en: 11 And, behold, the man clothed with linen, which had the inkhorn by his side, reported the matter, saying, I have done as thou hast commanded me.

9.7.1.en: In the Septuagint (Ezek 9:11) the man clothed with linen was girded. St. John Chrysostom comments on this, saying: [Being girded points to constant vigilance; therefore God commanded Job to gird up his loins (Job 38:3), and Moses and the prophets, and the Lord Himself appears girded.]

9.7.2.en: The prophet fell upon his face [8] when he saw the corpses of the priests and the people, and cried from the depths to God not to destroy the remnant when He poured out His wrath upon Jerusalem. The Lord answered him that He is girded with righteousness... Although He permitted the severe chastisement, He does not ignore the holy few, for He had said before: "Come not near any man upon whom is the mark" [6]... The cries of the prophet will not be lost, but he hears the divine voice: "I have done as thou hast commanded me" [11].

9.7.3.en: How great is the seal of the Spirit!

9.7.4.en: * How great is the seal of Your Holy Spirit upon me!

9.7.5.en: You sealed me with the mark in the sacrament of the Holy Myron, and so counted me as Your own possession!

9.7.6.en: Your cross on my forehead is the sign of spiritual soldiery, and upon it is the mark: "Holiness to the LORD!"

9.7.7.en: By You I have become fearsome; the enemy cannot crush me as long as I am with You!

9.7.8.en: * I fear lest my black garments condemn me; I dread lest I grow careless, hiding behind the garments of service!

9.7.9.en: Guard me, for I am in danger!

9.7.10.en: * You are wonderful, O Holy One; in chastisement You begin with Your priests. You are firm with Your disciples for their edification, yet You are the High Priest who works in them!

9.7.11.en: You are sweet and gentle even in Your chastisements; the wounds of Your chastisements are sweeter than the kisses of an enemy!

9.7.12.en: Let Your left hand chastise me and Your right hand embrace me, O Bridegroom of my soul!

10.0.0.en: 1 Then I looked, and, behold, in the firmament that was above the head of the cherubims there appeared over them as it were a sapphire stone, as the appearance of the likeness of a throne. 2 And he spake unto the man clothed with linen, and said, Go in between the wheels, even under the cherub, and fill thine hand with coals of fire from between the cherubims, and scatter them over the city. And he went in in my sight. 3 Now the cherubims stood on the right side of the house, when the man went in; and the cloud filled the inner court. 4 Then the glory of the LORD went up from the cherub, and stood over the threshold of the house; and the house was filled with the cloud, and the court was full of the brightness of the LORD'S glory. 5 And the sound of the cherubims' wings was heard even to the outer court, as the voice of the almighty God when he speaketh. 6 And it came to pass, that when he had commanded the man clothed with linen, saying, Take fire from between the wheels, from between the cherubims; then he went in, and stood beside the wheels. 7 And one cherub stretched forth his hand from between the cherubims unto the fire that was between the cherubims, and took thereof, and put it into the hands of him that was clothed with linen: who took it, and went out. 8 And there appeared in the cherubims the form of a man's hand under their wings. 9 And when I looked, behold the four wheels by the cherubims, one wheel by one cherub, and another wheel by another cherub: and the appearance of the wheels was as the colour of a beryl stone. 10 And as for their appearances, they four had one likeness, as if a wheel had been in the midst of a wheel. 11 When they went, they went upon their four sides; they turned not as they went, but to the place whither the head looked they followed it; they turned not as they went. 12 And their whole body, and their backs, and their hands, and their wings, and the wheels, were full of eyes round about, even the wheels that they four had. 13 As for the wheels, it was cried unto them in my hearing, O wheel. 14 And every one had four faces: the first face was the face of a cherub, and the second face was the face of a man, and the third the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle. 15 And the cherubims were lifted up. This is the living creature that I saw by the river of Chebar. 16 And when the cherubims went, the wheels went by them: and when the cherubims lifted up their wings to mount up from the earth, the same wheels also turned not from beside them. 17 When they stood, these stood; and when they were lifted up, these lifted up themselves also: for the spirit of the living creature was in them.

10.0.1.en: Before the Lord announced His complete departure from His house, He revealed to His prophet the vision that He had shown him before by the river Chebar, that is, His fiery divine chariot, which he had earlier called "the likeness of the glory of the LORD." It was discussed in some detail in the first chapter, except that here he calls the living creatures "cherubim."

10.0.2.en: What is new in this vision is that he saw the man clothed with linen, who had the writer's inkhorn at his side, who marks those who sigh over the abominations of Jerusalem (chapter 9), enter between the wheels under the cherub, and command a cherub to fill his hands with coals of fire from between the cherubim and scatter them over the city to burn it.

10.0.3.en: We have said that the man clothed with linen is none other than "the Word of God incarnate," who came as a Priest, wearing the priestly garments to offer the sacrifice of His love for the salvation of humanity. His entering between the wheels is a declaration that He is the axis of the two Testaments: the Old Testament, or the Law, has Christ as its goal, and the New Testament, or the Gospel, is the revelation of the mystery of Jesus Christ... As for His going down under the cherubim, it is a declaration of the mystery of His Incarnation, as the Apostle Paul says: "Thou madest him a little lower than the angels" (Heb 2:7).

10.0.4.en: Some may ask: If the Lord came for our salvation, why does He command a cherub to take fire and cast it upon the city?

10.0.5.en: A. In this is a declaration of the fire of the mystical sacrifice. Although the Lord came forward as a Priest, at the same time He came forward as a sacrifice, bearing the wages of our sins - He who knew no sin - before bearing its fire that destroys the city, yet it is powerless to destroy Him!! Therefore in the week of the Holy Passion the Church focuses on the prophecies of the Old Testament that show the ugliness of sin and its destructive effects, in order to reveal the love of Christ who bore the sins of the world. And the more the Holy Spirit shows the human soul the deadly fruit of sin, the more it clings to Him who bore this fruit in its place.

10.0.6.en: B. Perhaps this fire also symbolizes the fiery Holy Spirit, whom the Lord Christ sent to us from the Father to burn up the corruption of sin, demolishing in us the old city, or the old man, and establishing a new city, or a new inner temple, in which the Lord dwells.

10.0.7.en: C. This act was a declaration of the burning of the city by the Babylonians (2 Kgs 25:9) at the hand of Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard and servant of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon... For when the holy city abandoned holiness of life, it deserved destruction at the hands of the Gentile enemies.

10.1.0.en: It is noted that when the Lord entered between the cherubim, the cloud filled the outer court, as though by the Son's entering into the Incarnation He declared His glory among us, who were outside. He says: "And the sound of the cherubims' wings was heard even to the outer court, as the voice of the almighty God when he speaketh" [5], as though the voice of the Almighty God reached us who were outside, by the coming of the Word to us.

10.2.0.en: "They turned not as they went, but to the place whither the head looked they followed it" [11]. So the wheel of God's chariot goes behind the Head, that is, according to a divine plan; no man, nor any creature at all, will be able to challenge God. On His divine throne He grants grace and mercy to those who seek them, and issues sentence and judgment upon those who oppose Him. Who can challenge God?!

10.3.0.en: His chariot is full of eyes round about [12]; it does not move at random, for His judgment is just and true. He is the One who looks upon the hearts and searches the reins... and nothing is hidden from Him!

10.4.s.en: 2. The departure of the divine glory from the house of the Lord:

10.4.0.en: 18 Then the glory of the LORD departed from off the threshold of the house, and stood over the cherubims. 19 And the cherubims lifted up their wings, and mounted up from the earth in my sight: when they went out, the wheels also were beside them, and every one stood at the door of the east gate of the LORD'S house; and the glory of the God of Israel was over them above. 20 This is the living creature that I saw under the God of Israel by the river of Chebar; and I knew that they were the cherubims. 21 Every one had four faces apiece, and every one four wings; and the likeness of the hands of a man was under their wings. 22 And the likeness of their faces was the same faces which I saw by the river of Chebar, their appearances and themselves: they went every one straight forward.

10.4.1.en: "Then the glory of the LORD departed from off the threshold of the house, and stood over the cherubims. And the cherubims lifted up their wings, and mounted up from the earth in my sight" [18]. The prophet affirmed that he saw the glory of the Lord leaving His house, as He departed with His fiery chariot far from the people who rejected the divine glory. It was not possible for the Lord to dwell where man is determined to do evil, "for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness? And what concord hath Christ with Belial?" (2 Cor 6:14-15).

10.4.2.en: The Lord had to depart from His old temple, which insisted on denial, in order to establish in us a new temple made by His Holy Spirit. Origen speaks of it, saying: [Let the soul have an altar in the midst of the heart, upon which the sacrifices of prayer and the burnt offerings of mercy are offered; upon it let the bulls of pride be slain with the knife of meekness, and the rams of anger and the goats of luxury and lusts be killed on it... Let the soul know how to set up within itself the holy of holies of its heart as a lampstand that shines without ceasing.]

10.4.3.en: The prophet saw the glory of the Shekinah going out on the threshold of the house and rising to the heavens, but he saw that the glory stopped for a while above the entrance of the east gate, as though awaiting a last opportunity, even after leaving the place, in case they might repent and He would return. He departs from His house to ascend to heaven without suffering any loss, but He seeks the benefit of humanity, its salvation and its glory! The Apostle Paul expressed this by saying: "Grieve not the Holy Spirit!"

10.4.4.en: How marvelous! While the wicked man does all he can that God may depart from his life, God does not want His glory to depart from the heart of man, giving countless opportunities that He may work in him!

10.4.5.en: Would that Your glory might not depart from me!

10.4.6.en: * You have no need of my small heart, for heaven and earth are full of Your glory!

10.4.7.en: I am the one who needs Your glory not to depart from me, You whom all the heavenly beings glorify!

10.4.8.en: * I confess to You with my tears and the sighs of my heart!

10.4.9.en: By my sins and iniquities I drive Your glory out from within me, I grieve Your Holy Spirit who dwells in me!

10.4.10.en: But You do not want Your glory to depart from my heart!

10.4.11.en: * You have no need to reveal Your glory within me, but Your wondrous love longs to reveal it in me!

10.4.12.en: Be glorified within me, that I may be made worthy of the fellowship of Your eternal glory!
